summary: An anthology of American fake-doctor cases, chiefly a Toledo couple who falsely diagnosed dozens of patients with Alzheimer's to bill Medicare, that exposes how easily provider numbers are faked and how private health insurers ignore fraud.

evidence.note: Love-Robinson poses as a doctor at a West Palm Beach hospital in winter 2014-15
Jenkinses open a cognitive center at the Toledo Clinic in November 2013
scheme of billing Medicare for tests and false Alzheimer's diagnoses under the husband's NPI
coconut oil prescribed as Alzheimer's treatment; host debunks the fad
FBI probe, more than sixty victims, both convicted and sentenced to prison
Williams born in Idaho around 1963; early career and a failed gym investment scheme
Williams ramps up NPI fraud from 2014, holding twenty NPIs by 2017
family tips to Aetna, Cigna and UnitedHealthcare go nowhere
ProPublica finding that private insurers rarely report or pursue fraud
closing segment on a fake UCLA resident who later earned a real MD

notes: Anthology episode. Part 2's title names health insurers as the real bastards, so the industry is a second primary subject; no single company fits, so it is entered as a generic organization (low fit). Williams treated as secondary despite a long segment, which keeps his 1963 birth out of the covered span. Covered span starts around his 1992 marriage and teaching job. Love-Robinson's birth year and the Jenkins sentencing years are inferred, not stated.
